speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower with regard to the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) (a) which are the top five sectors and industries on the FCF Watchlist; (b) what are the most common job categories and their salary ranges on the Watchlist; and (c) what measures will be implemented to facilitate senior job opportunities for Singapore Citizens in critical sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) also engages these firms to offer assistance to improve their hiring practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the other end of the spectrum, we recognise employers with exemplary human resource (HR) practices as our Human Capital Partners (HCPartners).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: HCPartners actively groom Singaporeans for senior positions, through initiatives, such as management trainee programmes, overseas assignments and postings, as well as job rotations, across different business functions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, HCPartners have a healthy local workforce share at all levels, including at senior levels.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Additionally, the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) supports employers in developing the next generation of Singaporean leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through the programme, Singaporeans will acquire leadership competencies and critical experiences to take on senior positions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I just want to ask the Minister since the update during the Committee of Supply (COS) on the number of companies that are on the FCF Watchlist, which is 350, has there been an increase or a decrease?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Likewise, because of the new broadened coverage of the FCF with effect from 1 July this year, what is the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) seeing?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Has there been an increase or a decrease in the number of Watchlist companies?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We continue to work with each one of them to improve their hiring practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As and when we are told of companies that have practices that are suspected to be discriminatory, TAFEP will engage the companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our intent is really to help them improve their practices in order to be fairer and more progressive towards Singaporeans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the number that we work with is not a fixed target, but it does give an indication of the intensity of the effort that we are applying.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question which the Member asked relates to the advertising requirement under FCF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have also requested more companies to be covered under FCF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, as it stands right now, the advertising requirement would already cover the large majority of jobs at the PMET level.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to monitor and make sure that FCF remains credible.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Are they still eligible for Government funding, such as Adapt and Grow and all the others, to improve their businesses?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Are they still eligible to apply for those kinds of fundings?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think we try not to conflate the two.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the scheme is beneficial to the companies, if the scheme can benefit our citizens, I do not see why we should prevent them from doing so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Having said that, generally speaking, if the firms are on the Watchlist, I think they have multiple issues, and it is not quite likely that they are at the same time looking at application to the other schemes to support various human resource initiatives.
